trails.name: Rooster
trails.name_note: ชื่อตาม component set ใน Figma (ยังไม่มีชื่อแสดงผลที่ออกแบบไว้ — O/P-2xx)
trails.description: Few animals have lived as closely alongside the peoples of Southeast Asia as the chicken. Descended from the region's wild red junglefowl, it became part of farming, ritual, artisanship and household life. This trail explores the transformation of this familiar fowl into an enduring expression of protection, prosperity and renewal.

trails.name: Turtle
trails.name_note: ชื่อตาม component set ใน Figma (ยังไม่มีชื่อแสดงผลที่ออกแบบไว้ — O/P-2xx)
trails.description: Living in rivers, wetlands, mangroves and seas, turtles have long inspired communities across Southeast Asia. Represented in various cultural contexts, from temple foundations and ritual objects to maritime traditions and household ornaments, turtles are enduring symbols of protection, continuity and the connections between land and water.

trails.name: Deer
trails.name_note: ชื่อตาม component set ใน Figma (ยังไม่มีชื่อแสดงผลที่ออกแบบไว้ — O/P-2xx)
trails.description: Deer have lived alongside the peoples of Southeast Asia's forests and woodlands for millennia. Across the region, the relationships between communities and the environments they inhabit have given rise to stories, artistic traditions and material culture, contributing to the region’s shared heritage.

trails.name: Dragon
trails.name_note: ชื่อตาม component set ใน Figma (ยังไม่มีชื่อแสดงผลที่ออกแบบไว้ — O/P-2xx)
trails.description: Over centuries of trade, migration and cultural exchange, dragon imagery travelled with people and communities from China across the seas to Southeast Asia, bringing with it the associations the dragon represented, including heavenly power, authority, water and rainfall.

trails.name: Fish
trails.name_note: ชื่อตาม component set ใน Figma (ยังไม่มีชื่อแสดงผลที่ออกแบบไว้ — O/P-2xx)
trails.description: Life in Southeast Asia has been shaped by water. Rivers, seas, mangroves and wetlands have sustained communities for thousands of years, while the creatures that inhabit them have inspired stories and have been incorporated into objects of everyday life and rituals. This trail explores how fish and aquatic mammals reveal enduring relationships between people, water and the natural world.

trails.name: Hornbill
trails.name_note: ชื่อตาม component set ใน Figma (ยังไม่มีชื่อแสดงผลที่ออกแบบไว้ — O/P-2xx)
trails.description: Living high in the forest canopy, hornbills have long shaped the ecological and cultural landscapes of Southeast Asia. This trail shows how communities in Southeast Asia have incorporated the hornbill and its associated meanings into ceremonies, art and everyday life.

trails.name: Horse
trails.name_note: ชื่อตาม component set ใน Figma (ยังไม่มีชื่อแสดงผลที่ออกแบบไว้ — O/P-2xx)
trails.description: While horses are not native to Southeast Asia, they travelled with the region's peoples over centuries via trade and warfare. By joining diverse communities, they became part of beliefs and artistic traditions across the region. Today, they reveal how shared heritage emerges through movement, encounter and cultural exchange.

trails.name: Naga
trails.name_note: ชื่อตาม component set ใน Figma (ยังไม่มีชื่อแสดงผลที่ออกแบบไว้ — O/P-2xx)
trails.description: Long before the Naga became part of Southeast Asia's religious traditions, communities across the region revered serpents as guardians of water, fertility and the natural world. This trail explores how these longstanding relationships have shaped ritual, art and everyday life.

trails.name: Water bird
trails.name_note: ชื่อตาม component set ใน Figma (ยังไม่มีชื่อแสดงผลที่ออกแบบไว้ — O/P-2xx)
trails.description: Communities in Southeast Asia have long shared with waterbirds the places where rivers meet the sea, and the coasts, wetlands and floodplains of the region. This trail explores how knowledge of these birds, gained through close observation, gave rise to stories, rituals and objects that continue to connect people with the region's waterscapes.

trails.name: Makara
trails.name_note: ชื่อตาม component set ใน Figma (ยังไม่มีชื่อแสดงผลที่ออกแบบไว้ — O/P-2xx)
trails.description: What happens when communities combine the qualities of different animals into a single mythical being? Inspired by the crocodile and other creatures of land and water, the makara became one of Southeast Asia's enduring guardians. This trail follows how communities reimagined the makara through ritual, architecture and everyday life.

trails.name: Lion
trails.name_note: ชื่อตาม component set ใน Figma (ยังไม่มีชื่อแสดงผลที่ออกแบบไว้ — O/P-2xx)
trails.description: While lions have never inhabited Southeast Asia, communities across the region incorporated them into their artistic, religious and material traditions. Reimagined through local beliefs and practices, the lion is part of the region’s shared heritage, which emerged through creativity, encounter and cultural exchange.

trails.name: Seashell
trails.name_note: ชื่อตาม component set ใน Figma (ยังไม่มีชื่อแสดงผลที่ออกแบบไว้ — O/P-2xx)
trails.description: Seashells and marine invertebrates, such as giant clams and sponges, were transported throughout Southeast Asia over centuries as ornaments, currency, ritual objects and works of art. This trail follows their remarkable journeys, revealing how communities transformed seashells and marine invertebrates into enduring expressions of belief and identity.

trails.name: Buffalo
trails.name_note: ชื่อตาม component set ใน Figma (ยังไม่มีชื่อแสดงผลที่ออกแบบไว้ — O/P-2xx)
trails.description: The water buffalo (Bubalus bubalis) has lived alongside the peoples of Southeast Asia for centuries. Domesticated from wild ancestors, it became an indispensable companion in monsoon agriculture, wet-rice fields and the village economies that sustained communities across the region. Through its role in farming and daily life, the buffalo has helped shape both the landscapes and livelihoods of Southeast Asia.

trails.name: Phoenix
trails.name_note: ชื่อตาม component set ใน Figma (ยังไม่มีชื่อแสดงผลที่ออกแบบไว้ — O/P-2xx)
trails.description: In Chinese tradition, the fenghuang (phoenix) is a composite creature with the neck of a snake, the breast of a swallow, the back of a tortoise, the tail of a fish and five-coloured plumage; a mythical bird whose harmonious form no single species could embody alone.

trails.name: Bird
trails.name_note: ชื่อตาม component set ใน Figma (ยังไม่มีชื่อแสดงผลที่ออกแบบไว้ — O/P-2xx)
trails.description: In Southeast Asia, birds feature as integral elements of the region's cultural heritage, serving as symbols of national identity and spirituality. Communities across the region view birds as protectors and companions and as representing the connections between nature, belief and everyday life.

trails.name: Garuda
trails.name_note: ชื่อตาม component set ใน Figma (ยังไม่มีชื่อแสดงผลที่ออกแบบไว้ — O/P-2xx)
trails.description: Garuda is a mythical bird-human creature inspired by close observation of real birds of prey. Its ancient rivalry with serpents echoes the relationship in nature in which large raptors prey upon snakes. Communities observing this relationship came to understand powerful birds as protectors against creatures that are sometimes associated with danger. Garuda, a great bird-like being and the mount of Vishnu, is one of Hindu mythology's most enduring figures; embodying strength, knowledge, courage and discipline.

trails.name: Elephant
trails.name_note: ชื่อตาม component set ใน Figma (ยังไม่มีชื่อแสดงผลที่ออกแบบไว้ — O/P-2xx)
trails.description: Elephants have lived alongside the peoples of South-East Asia for millennia, shaping forests and contributing to livelihoods, beliefs and artistic traditions. Across the region, communities have interpreted the elephant in various ways but have nevertheless created a shared heritage rooted in long-term relationships between people, animals and the environments they inhabit.
